To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

business managers from the Arab Gulf region value balance and moderation, a concern for the negotiation outcome of the counterpart, motivation to create a “win-win” situation, honesty, trust and trust worthiness.

business negotiators from the Middle East value the following components in a negotiation: (1) the ability to reach a balanced agreement, (2) concern for the counterpart, (3) motivation to create a mutually satisfactory outcome, (4) honesty, (5) patience, (6) trust and (7) trustworthiness.

(a) the subjective value structure of business managers from Oman includes the following components, in order of importance: balance and moderation; (b) concern for the negotiation outcome of the counterpart; (c) the motivation to create win-win situations; (d) honesty; (e) patience; (f) trust and trustworthness; and (g) that the subjective value structures of business negotiators in the Arabian Gulf are different from the value structures of business managers in other cultures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the subjective value structure of Middle Eastern Arab negotiators.
the subjective value structure of business managers when they negotiate.
the subjective value structure of business negotiators in the Middle East.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the value of the outcome of negotiation in terms of a win-win situation and the value of the process in terms of the development of a relationship with the counterpart is the most important value of negotiation in the Arab world.
business managers in Oman are concerned with the subjective value structure of the negotiation process and outcomes, which is in line with the findings of previous research in the field.
Arab business managers in Oman value the subjective outcomes that are consistent with the cultural values of their own society.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the subjective value of the negotiation outcome is a complex and multifaceted construct.
we are not only interested in what we value but also how we value what we value.
we have identified a number of important factors that business managers in Oman value when they negotiate.
The main takeaway from our work is that

managers should not assume that the value structures that underlie the negotiation process are universal and that they should be aware of the potential impact of their own values on the negotiation process.
business managers in the Arabian Gulf are not only concerned about achieving a win for their own organization, they also want to achieve a win for the other party.
business managers in the Arabian Gulf value a number of social psychological outcomes when negotiating with their counterparts.
